name: George Washington
fact: Unanimous choice of the Electoral College — twice. Turned down anything resembling a crown and went home to farm.
reckoning: Enslaved more than 300 people at Mount Vernon, signed the Fugitive Slave Act of 1793, and pursued those who escaped him, including Ona Judge.

name: John Adams
fact: First to live in the White House. As a young lawyer, defended the British soldiers of the Boston Massacre — and won.
reckoning: The Alien and Sedition Acts jailed editors and journalists for criticizing his administration.

name: Thomas Jefferson
fact: Wrote the Declaration, doubled the country with the Louisiana Purchase, died July 4, 1826 — fifty years to the day.
reckoning: Wrote 'all men are created equal' while enslaving more than 600 people — including Sally Hemings and children who were his own.

name: James Madison
fact: Father of the Constitution. Smallest president, largest framework.
reckoning: Enslaved over 100 people while drafting liberty's framework, and freed none of them, not even in his will.

name: James Monroe
fact: The Monroe Doctrine and the Era of Good Feelings. Also died on July 4. The founders kept doing that.
reckoning: A lifelong slaveholder; his colonization project aimed to remove free Black Americans from the country, not to free the enslaved.

name: John Quincy Adams
fact: Son of a president. Argued the Amistad case before the Supreme Court after leaving office — and won.
reckoning: As president and diplomat, advanced treaties and expansion that dispossessed Native nations of their land.

name: Andrew Jackson
fact: First populist president. His parrot was reportedly removed from his funeral for swearing.
reckoning: Signed the Indian Removal Act — the Trail of Tears followed. Enslaved about 150 people and once offered 'ten dollars extra for every hundred lashes' to an escapee's captor.

name: Martin Van Buren
fact: First president born a U.S. citizen. The word 'OK' may trace to his nickname, Old Kinderhook.
reckoning: The Trail of Tears was largely carried out on his watch, and he defended the policy to the end.

name: William Henry Harrison
fact: 31 days in office. The two-hour inaugural address in the freezing rain did not help.
reckoning: As governor of Indiana Territory, extracted treaties that stripped millions of acres from Native nations, by whiskey and by pressure.

name: John Tyler
fact: First vice president to succeed to the office — and he made sure the precedent stuck.
reckoning: Died a member of the Confederate Congress — Washington officially ignored his death as that of a man in rebellion.

name: James K. Polk
fact: Promised one term and four goals. Delivered all four and left.
reckoning: A slaveholder who bought children while in the White House, and engineered the Mexican-American War on a pretext Lincoln stood up in Congress to call a lie.

name: Zachary Taylor
fact: Forty years a soldier; reportedly never voted in a presidential election before his own.
reckoning: Enslaved more than 100 people on his Louisiana and Mississippi plantations.

name: Millard Fillmore
fact: Last Whig president. Installed the White House's first permanent library.
reckoning: Signed the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850, drafting the whole North into the business of hunting escaped human beings.

name: Franklin Pierce
fact: Recited his entire inaugural address from memory — 3,319 words.
reckoning: Championed the Kansas-Nebraska Act, opening new territory to slavery — 'Bleeding Kansas' was the bill's first harvest.

name: James Buchanan
fact: The only bachelor president. Watched the Union crack and handed Lincoln the pieces.
reckoning: Lobbied the Supreme Court toward Dred Scott, blamed abolitionists for the crisis, and watched secession begin without lifting a hand.

name: Abraham Lincoln
fact: Preserved the Union, freed the slaves, and needed only 272 words at Gettysburg.
reckoning: Suspended habeas corpus, long endorsed colonization of freed Black Americans, and approved the largest mass execution in U.S. history — 38 Dakota men at Mankato, 1862.

name: Andrew Johnson
fact: First president impeached — acquitted by a single vote.
reckoning: Sabotaged Reconstruction at every turn — vetoed civil rights bills and let white rule rebuild itself in the South.

name: Ulysses S. Grant
fact: Won the war, then raced death to finish his memoirs and provide for his family. He won that too.
reckoning: His administration drowned in corruption scandals, and his 1862 General Order No. 11 expelled Jews 'as a class' from his military district — an order he spent years regretting.

name: Rutherford B. Hayes
fact: Won by one electoral vote. His wife banned alcohol from the White House — 'Lemonade Lucy.'
reckoning: The Compromise of 1877 traded Reconstruction away for the presidency — federal troops left the South, and Jim Crow moved in.

name: James A. Garfield
fact: Could reportedly write Latin with one hand and Greek with the other — at the same time.
reckoning: Two hundred days. The record is thin on both counts — he ran on rights for Black citizens and died before the promise could be tested.

name: Chester A. Arthur
fact: The machine politician who signed civil-service reform anyway. Nobody was more surprised than the machine.
reckoning: Signed the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 — the first federal law to ban immigrants by race and nation.

name: Grover Cleveland
fact: The first president to serve two non-consecutive terms. Hold that thought until #24.
reckoning: Signed the Dawes Act, which broke up tribal lands and stripped Native nations of some 90 million acres.

name: Benjamin Harrison
fact: Electricity was installed in the White House on his watch — he and his wife were afraid to touch the switches.
reckoning: The Wounded Knee massacre happened on his watch — and his government pinned Medals of Honor on the soldiers who carried it out.

name: Grover Cleveland
fact: Told you. The same Grover Cleveland, back by popular demand — literally.
reckoning: Back in office, he sent federal troops to crush the Pullman Strike, killing workers to move the mail.

name: William McKinley
fact: Ran the famous front-porch campaign — the voters came to him.
reckoning: Annexed the Philippines and started the war to keep it — at least 200,000 Filipino civilians died.

name: Theodore Roosevelt
fact: Youngest president ever. The teddy bear is named for him. Spoke softly; the stick, famously, was big.
reckoning: Believed sincerely in racial hierarchy; dishonorably discharged 167 Black soldiers at Brownsville on evidence that was never there.

name: William Howard Taft
fact: Later Chief Justice of the United States — the only person to lead two branches of government.
reckoning: Ran the Philippine occupation and called its people 'little brown brothers' — empire wearing a paternal smile.

name: Woodrow Wilson
fact: Nobel Peace Prize for the League of Nations. Also the only president with a Ph.D.
reckoning: Resegregated the federal civil service, screened 'The Birth of a Nation' at the White House, and jailed dissenters — including Eugene Debs — under the Espionage and Sedition Acts.

name: Warren G. Harding
fact: Won by promising a 'return to normalcy' — a word his critics insisted was not one.
reckoning: Teapot Dome: his friends sold the nation's oil reserves for bribes in black bags.

name: Calvin Coolidge
fact: Silent Cal. A dinner guest bet she could get more than two words out of him. 'You lose.'
reckoning: Signed the Immigration Act of 1924 — race quotas engineered to shut out Italians, Jews, and all of Asia.

name: Herbert Hoover
fact: Fed millions in postwar Europe before the Crash made his name a shantytown.
reckoning: Sent the Army with tanks and tear gas against the Bonus Army — veterans camped in the capital asking to be paid — and began the 'repatriation' drives that expelled up to a million people of Mexican descent, many of them citizens.

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
fact: Four terms — the reason the 22nd Amendment exists. Fireside chats, the New Deal, the war.
reckoning: Executive Order 9066 imprisoned 120,000 Japanese Americans, most of them citizens; the St. Louis and its Jewish refugees were turned back to Europe on his watch.

name: Harry S. Truman
fact: The buck stopped there. Held up the wrong headline, grinning like a man who'd read the right one.
reckoning: Ordered the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki — more than 200,000 dead, most of them civilians. History still argues the necessity; the dead do not.

name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
fact: Supreme Allied Commander on D-Day; built the interstate highway system in peacetime.
reckoning: The CIA overthrew elected governments in Iran and Guatemala on his orders; Executive Order 10450 purged thousands of gay Americans from federal service; 'Operation Wetback' deported en masse.

name: John F. Kennedy
fact: Youngest elected president. Promised the Moon within the decade — delivery arrived on schedule, 1969.
reckoning: Authorized the FBI's wiretaps on Martin Luther King Jr., owned the Bay of Pigs, and walked the country deeper into Vietnam.

name: Lyndon B. Johnson
fact: Civil Rights Act, Voting Rights Act, Medicare — passed by pure applied force of personality.
reckoning: Escalated Vietnam on the Gulf of Tonkin's false pretenses — 58,000 Americans and well over a million Vietnamese died in the war he chose not to lose.

name: Richard Nixon
fact: Opened China, created the EPA, and remains the only president to resign the office.
reckoning: Watergate. Also: the secret bombing of Cambodia, and a drug war his own aide admitted was built to criminalize Black Americans and the antiwar left.

name: Gerald Ford
fact: The only president never elected president or vice president. The Constitution has a footnote just for him.
reckoning: Pardoned Nixon before any charge could be tried, and gave Indonesia the green light to invade East Timor days before it happened.

name: Jimmy Carter
fact: Brokered the Camp David Accords; won the Nobel Peace Prize 21 years after leaving office.
reckoning: The human-rights presidency had asterisks: arms kept flowing to Indonesia mid-atrocity, and the Shah kept American backing nearly to the fall.

name: Ronald Reagan
fact: The Great Communicator. 'Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall.'
reckoning: Stayed publicly silent on AIDS for years while thousands died; Iran-Contra sold missiles to Iran to illegally fund the Contras; the drug war's mass-incarceration era began in earnest here.

name: George H. W. Bush
fact: One of the Navy's youngest aviators in WWII; celebrated his 90th birthday by skydiving.
reckoning: Pardoned the Iran-Contra principals on his way out the door, burying the case; his campaign's Willie Horton ad set the standard for racial fear politics.

name: Bill Clinton
fact: Presided over the longest peacetime economic expansion to that point. Plays the saxophone.
reckoning: The 1994 crime bill helped build mass incarceration; welfare 'reform' and bank deregulation aged badly; lied under oath and was impeached for it.

name: George W. Bush
fact: The bullhorn at Ground Zero. Took up portrait painting after office — mostly of veterans.
reckoning: Invaded Iraq over weapons that were not there — hundreds of thousands died; authorized torture and called it 'enhanced interrogation'; Katrina drowned while FEMA fumbled.

name: Barack Obama
fact: First African American president. It started with one convention speech in 2004.
reckoning: Expanded drone warfare with a personal kill list that included a U.S. citizen — and, two weeks later, the citizen's 16-year-old son; deported more people than any president before him; Guantanamo never closed.

name: Donald Trump
fact: First president with no prior government or military service.
reckoning: Impeached twice — for pressuring Ukraine to smear a rival, and for January 6. The family-separation policy took thousands of children from their parents at the border.

name: Joe Biden
fact: Oldest president at inauguration; 36 years a senator before the White House.
reckoning: The Afghanistan withdrawal collapsed into chaos — thirteen service members and some 170 Afghans died at Abbey Gate; many border policies he campaigned against, he kept.

name: Donald Trump
fact: The second president with non-consecutive terms. Somewhere, Grover Cleveland finally has company.
reckoning: Took office as the first president with a felony record — convicted on 34 counts in New York in 2024, months before the election.
